documentNotes.title: Instructions
documentNotes.statement:
*The main problem and the two exercises are completely independent and can be solved in any order.*

*All the answers must be given in English or French. The clarity and precision will be taken into account for the final note.*

*The exam is 4 hours long! The calculators are authorized.*

problems.title: Some aspects of the astronautics
problems.statement:
The main goal of this problem is to obtain numerical values. An analytical expression of the result as a function of the given parameters should be given, but it’s just a bypass to the final solution.

**I – Propulsion by reaction.**

In this part we will study the principle of propulsion. To this end, we will consider a board with wheels or a trolley on which we have a machinist and ***n*** sacks filled with sand and of individual masse ***m*** everyone. We neglect all dissipative effects. In order to simplify the expressions, we will also neglect the masse of the trolley and the machinist itself compared to the masse of every sand-bag. The referential system ***R***, attached to the ***Ox*** axis is galilean.

figures.alt: Two drawings side by side. Left: a trolley (flat board) on an axis x pointing left with origin O on the right, carrying a pyramid of ten round sacks and a stick-figure machinist standing at rest. Right: the same trolley after a throw, with nine sacks; the machinist has thrown one sack to the right, labelled u/chariot with an arrow to the right, and the trolley moves to the left with velocity V1 (arrow to the left); axis x and origin O below.

parts.label: I.A
parts.statement:
At time $t = 0$, the operator throw out the first sack of masse $m$, with speed $\mathbf{u} = -u\mathbf{e}_x{}^{*}$ compared to the speed of the board! Show that, in the referential $R$ attached to the ground (to the $Ox$ axis), the impulsion of one system (which you should define precisely) is conserved. Using this general property, find the speed $\mathbf{V_1}$ (evaluated in $R$) of the trolley and all that is on it, after this first throw.

$^{*}$ Every symbol in bold should be considered as a vector variable.

parts.label: I.B
parts.statement: At time $t_2 = t_1 + T$, the machinist throw out a second sack, with speed $\mathbf{u} = -u\mathbf{e}_x$ compared to the speed of the board! Evaluate the speed (in $R$) of the trolley and all that is on it, after this second throw. Show that it could be rewritten as $\mathbf{V}_2 = -\left(\dfrac{1}{n-1} + \dfrac{1}{n-2}\right)\mathbf{u}$. Define the studied system.

parts.label: I.C
parts.statement: Establish the expression of the speed $\mathbf{V}_k$ of the trolley, always evaluated in the referential $R$, after the $k$-th throw effectuated at time $t_1 + (k-1)T$, as a function of $n, k$ and $\mathbf{u}$. Define the studied system.

parts.label: I.D
parts.statement: Establish the expression $\mathbf{a}_k$ of the average acceleration of the trolley during a period of time including the $k$-th throw (for instance, between $t_1 + (k - 3/2)T$ and $t_1 + (k - 1/2)T$) as a function of $n, k, T$ and $\mathbf{u}$ (in $R$).

parts.label: I.E
parts.statement: We call $D_m$ the “outflow of masse” or “masse debit”, which is the masse thrown out of the trolley per time unit. Express $\mathbf{a}_k$ as a function of $n, k, D_m, m$ and $\mathbf{u}$.

parts.label: I.F
parts.statement: Show that the system $\{$trolley and all that it contains after the $k$-th throw$\}$ seems to be exposed, during a period of time including the throw, to a pushing force $\Pi$ average that you should express as a function of $D_m$ and $\mathbf{u}$.
parts.statementAfter:
**II – Propulsion by a rocket engine.**

Now, we will study of a total masse (at the moment $t$) $m(t)$ and speed $\mathbf{V}(t)$ in a galilean referential $R$; we suppose that the “outflow of masse” $D_m$ of the effected gas is constant and that the speed of ejection is $\mathbf{u}$ in the referential $R'$ attached to the rocket. All the external forces are represented by one force noted $\mathbf{R}$.

parts.label: II.A
parts.statement: By making a detailed balance of the impulsion of one closed system between the time $t$ and $t + dt$, show that $m(t)\dfrac{d\mathbf{V}(t)}{dt} = \mathbf{R} + \mathbf{T}$, where $\mathbf{T}$ is a “pushing force”, which expression you should precise by means of $\mathbf{u}$ and $D_m$.

parts.label: II.B
parts.statement: We suppose that the rocket is moving in the empty space, we neglect all gravitational forces; the initial and final masse of the rocket is respectively $m_i$ and $m_f$; $\mathbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{V}(t)$ have the same fixed direction. Give the increase of the speed $\Delta V = V_f - V_i$ as a function of $m_i, m_f$ and $u$ where $u$ is the norm of $\mathbf{u}$ supposed constant.

parts.label: II.C
parts.statement: We define the propulsion efficiency $Q$ as the ratio of the kinetic energy, communicated to the “useful masse” $m_f$ of a rocket accelerated from a stand still position, to the total energy that is used, defined as $m_e u^2/2$, where $m_e$ is the ejected mass between the initial and the final moment. Give the expression of $Q$ as a function of $x = V_f/u$. Draw $Q$ as a function of $x$. How can you explain qualitatively the existence of a maximum?

parts.label: II.D
parts.statement: The total initial masse of the rocket Saturn V was $2\times 10^{6}\ \mathrm{kg}$, the speed of ejection of the gases was $4\ \mathrm{km.s^{-1}}$ and the take-off acceleration about $1g$ ($g \cong 10\ \mathrm{m.s^{-2}}$). Evaluate the “masse outflow” and discuss.
parts.statementAfter: In all the preceding questions the referential $R$ ($Oxyz$) is attached to the earth.

parts.label: II.E
parts.statement: At $t = 0$, a rocket without initial speed, situated at $z = 0$ is ignited. We suppose that the rocket is ascending vertically in a gravitational field $\mathbf{g}$ (supposed constant), with a “masse outflow” $D_m$, also supposed constant. The planet is without atmosphere. Find the expression giving the evolution of the speed $V(t)$ and the altitude $z(t)$ as a function of $m(0), g, u$ and $D_m$. We remind you that $\int \ln x dx = x\ln(x) - x$.

parts.label: II.F
parts.statement: The radius of the Earth is $R_T = 6400\ \mathrm{km}$. The intensity of the Earth’s gravity on the surface is $\mathrm{g}_0$ ($\mathrm{g}_0 \cong 10\ \mathrm{m.s^{-2}}$). Evaluate the potential energy of a masse of 1kg. at rest on the Earth surface, supposing its potential energy at infinity as zero.

parts.label: II.G
parts.statement: The energy produced by the combustion of one kilogram of dioxygen and dihydrogen mixture is less than $2\times 10^{7}\ \mathrm{J}$. In these conditions, is it possible to overcome the gravitation field of the Earth? We ask for a qualitative analysis.
parts.statementAfter:
**III. – The ionic engine.**

The ejection of matter could be done not only by a chemical, but also by an electrical way.

parts.label: III.A
parts.statement: Inside a spacecraft, charged particles of masse $\mu$ and positive charge $q$ are accelerated by a potential $U_t$ and after that ejected outside the spacecraft. Suppose that $D_m$ is the ejected “masse outflow”. Express the “pushing force” $T$ as a function of $q, U_t, D_m$ and $\mu$.

parts.label: III.B
parts.statement: In the case, where we neglect the gravitational force and the air resistance, evaluate the minimal electric power $P_{e\min}$ that the engine should supply, so that the acceleration of the spacecraft is $\gamma$. $P_{e\min}$ should be expressed as a function of $\gamma, \mu, q, U_t$ and the total instant masse $m$ of the spacecraft at the.

parts.label: III.C
parts.statement:
Numerical applications: The engine NSTAR in the probe Deep Space One, launched on 24 October 1998, had the following characteristics:

- Accelerating tension: $U_t = 1090\mathrm{V}$
- Consumed electrical power by the engine: $2{,}3\mathrm{kW}$
- Ejected particles: ions Xenon, charge $+e$ ($N_A = 6{,}02\times 10^{23}\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$, the molar masse of Xenon is $M_{Xe} = 131{,}3\mathrm{g.mol^{-1}}$, the elementary electrical charge is $e = 1{,}6\times 10^{-19}\mathrm{C}$)
- Pushing force: $93\mathrm{mN}$

Calculate the ratio $\mathrm{T/P_e}$ in two different ways. Is the provided data consistent? (an answer limited to “Yes” or “No” will be considered insufficient)

problems.title: Exercise 1
problems.statement: A plano-concave lens having index of refraction $n = 1{,}50$ is placed on a flat glass plate, as shown in ***Figure 1***. Its curved surface, with radius of curvature 8.00 m, is on the bottom. The lens is illuminated from above with yellow sodium light of wavelength 589 nm, and a series of concentric bright and dark rings is observed by reflection. The interference pattern has a dark spot at the center, surrounded by 50 dark rings, of which the largest is at the outer edge of the lens.

figures.caption: Figure 1
figures.alt: A plano-concave lens lying on a flat glass plate, its concave surface facing down so a thin air gap lies between them; orange rays come from above, one incident ray and two reflected rays going upward.

parts.label: (a)
parts.statement: What is the thickness of the air layer at the center of the interference pattern?

parts.label: (b)
parts.statement: Calculate the radius of the outermost dark ring.

parts.label: (c)
parts.statement: Find the focal length of the lens.

problems.title: Exercise 2
problems.statement: Consider a perfectly conducting disk of radius $r_0$ in a constant magnetic field $B$ perpendicular to the plane of the disk. Sliding contacts are provided at the edge of the disk ($C_1$) and at its axle ($C_2$) ( cf. ***Figure 2*** ). This system is Faraday’s “homopolar generator.” When turned at constant angular velocity, it provides a large direct current with no ripple. A torque is produced by a mass $M$ hung on a long string wrapped around the perimeter of the disk.

figures.caption: Figure 2
figures.alt: A grey conducting disk of radius r0 inside a dashed rectangle filled with crosses (magnetic field into the page). Sliding contact C1 touches the rim on the left and contact C2 the axle at the centre; wires from C1 and C2 lead down to a resistor R. A string wound on the rim on the right hangs down to a mass M below the field region.

parts.label: (a)
parts.statement: Explain. how and why a current flows. Give a quantitative expression for the current as a function of angular velocity.

parts.label: (b)
parts.statement: Given a long enough string, this system will reach a constant angular velocity $\omega_f$. Find this $\omega_f$ and the associated current.
